lede: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has triggered a political controversy after raising questions about former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud’s approach to judicial appointments. title: Begins at the base
standfirst: The persistence of caste in higher education cannot be addressed without tackling the greater inequality in schools, starting with universal, compulsory, free education in high-quality government schools.
lede: At Independence, the Indian higher education system was small, elitist, and socially exclusive, concentrated in a few institutions and dominated by the privileged castes, with limited access for Dalits, Adivasis, and women. By 2021–22, it had expanded to cover 1,168 universities, 45,473 colleges, and over 12,000 stand-alone institutions, enrolling 4.33 crore students. Yet, it still remains chronically underfunded, with public expenditure around 4 per cent of the GDP against the long-standing 6 per cent policy target.

title: For Delhi’s air pollution problem, stop blaming Punjab’s farmers
lede: Each autumn, a familiar script returns. Delhi’s air turns toxic, television crews travel to Punjab, satellite images of burning fields fill the screens, and the Punjabi farmer becomes the face of northern India’s winter smog. The smoke is real, and stubble burning does worsen early winter pollution. But a regional air pollution problem is repeatedly reduced to the image of a farmer setting a field on fire. The picture is complicated by the numbers. According to the Commission for Air Quality Management, Punjab’s officially recorded paddy stubble fire events fell from 71,304 in 2021 to 5,114 in 2025, a decline of about 93 per cent.

title: Column | The chicanery of Uncle-hood
standfirst: Years of lessons in integrity, undone by one uncle with a favour to ask
lede: Dear readers, you may find this hard to believe. But you are currently reading words written by a man who once almost became an officer of the Indian Administrative Services (IAS). And when I say “almost became”, I really mean that I applied for the exam, obtained a registration card, spent several weeks preparing for the exam, and then decided to never take the exam. This was some time in 2002 or 2003. My memory fails me. But yes, one day, in a fit of fury, I ripped my registration card into shreds and flung it out of a window in my maternal grandfather’s house.

title: United Nations' Report Flags Early Marriage As Major Barrier To Girls' Education Worldwide
standfirst: UNESCO found that India has achieved gender parity in urban areas, but only 59 girls completed upper secondary education for every 100 boys in rural areas.
lede: Gender parity in school enrolment has improved worldwide, but child marriage and early pregnancy continue to prevent many girls from completing their education, according to UNESCO's 2026 Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Gender Report. The report also flagged a sharp rural-urban divide in India, where girls in rural areas remain far less likely than boys to complete upper secondary education. As per the report, while gender gaps in education have narrowed and the share of girls married before 18 has decreased globally, very few girls return to school after giving birth in some regions, underscoring the need to end child marriage, prevent early pregnancies, and guarantee young mothers' right to continue their education.

standfirst: Former Israel Defense Forces chief Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a leading challenger to Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s October 27 election.
lede: Former Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as one of the principal challengers to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s October 27 general election, offering voters an alternative shaped by decades of military service and growing frustration over the government’s handling of national security. Eisenkot, 66, leads the centrist Yashar party, which has been polling ahead of Netanyahu’s Likud in several recent surveys. However, the election remains wide open. Israel’s 120-member Knesset requires a majority of at least 61 lawmakers to form a government, and polling suggests neither political camp has a guaranteed route to that threshold.

title: Cyclone Arnab: When will it hit Andhra Pradesh, which states are on alert and how severe will it be?
standfirst: The weather system developing over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm, with Andhra Pradesh facing a possible landfall on October 28.
lede: The weather system developing over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm, with Andhra Pradesh facing a possible landfall on October 28. Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are also preparing for heavy rainfall, strong winds and potential flooding. A depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, prompting authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha to step up disaster preparedness. The approaching storm, which will be named Cyclone Arnab once it reaches cyclonic storm intensity, is likely to bring winds of up to 140 kmph, heavy rainfall and possible flooding in vulnerable coastal areas.

title: India's First Bullet Train: 100-Foot-Deep Station, Undersea Tunnel Under Construction; Here's What's Cooking

lede: India's First Bullet Train: 100-Foot-Deep Station, Undersea Tunnel Under Construction; Here's What's Cooking There have been developments in India's first-ever bullet train project with ongoing construction of railway tracks, bridges, tunnels and stations on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad fast train corridor. According to India's Railway Minister, Ashwini Vaishnaw, the project which stretches to 508 km is making good progress, and the first train services are expected by the last quarter of 2027.

title: Tiger Shroff's Spokesperson Denies 'Why Was I Attacked' Statement After Firing Incident, Calls Reports 'Completely Untrue'
lede: Tiger Shroff’s spokesperson denied reports claiming that the actor questioned the motive behind the firing incident outside his residence in Mumbai. The clarification comes amid reports that Tiger had recorded his statement with the Mumbai Crime Branch following the October 18 incident. Reports had claimed that the actor was still in shock and did not wish to speak much about the incident. They also attributed a statement to him in which he questioned why anyone would target him. However, his spokesperson reportedly dismissed these claims, stating that Tiger has not made any such statement.
